newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Poland warns against superpower deal over NATO.
newsitem.headline: Poland warns against superpower deal over NATO.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, visiting NATO to push his country's membership plans forward, said he backed the idea of a NATO accord with Russia, but warned against a deal between superpowers.

"In a system of cooperative security, there is no place for geopolitics, spheres of influence, secret protocols or 'concerts of great powers'. We trust that our NATO partners share this view. We hope so does Russia," he said in a speech to NATO ambassadors.

He was speaking after U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Friday that the United States and Russia had made "very important progress" on an agreement between Moscow and the Western NATO alliance.
But she told a news conference after two days of talks with Russian officials that some very complex questions remained.

Cimoszewicz said that NATO's dialogue with Moscow, which deeply opposes the alliance's plans to expand to central and eastern European countries, should in no way limit the freedom of other countries to shape relations with NATO as they wish.

"The results of this dialogue should in no way limit the freedom of other nations to shape their relations with NATO according to their needs and aspirations -- neither today, nor in the future," he said.
He backed NATO's assertion that there was no question of stationing of nuclear weapons on the territories of new members of the alliance.
"We neither see the need to have them on our soil nor have any intention to change our position in the future," he said.

NATO intends to invite a number of central and eastern European countries to open membership talks at a summit in Madrid set for July 8-9. Poland, along with the Czech Republic and Hungary, are favourites to be in the first list of countries.
